root_text: Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) is not a new virus and has been reported worldwide previously. It has been known since the early 2000s and has been attributed as a cause of respiratory infection, for possibly even longer🧵

nodes.author: GSRajahram
nodes.text: Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) is not a new virus and has been reported worldwide previously. It has been known since the early 2000s and has been attributed as a cause of respiratory infection, for possibly even longer🧵

nodes.author: GSRajahram
nodes.text: For most people, it is associated with a mild self-limiting illness of cough, nasal congestion, running nose, sore throat, and fever and is know to be prevalent in children. 2/5

nodes.author: GSRajahram
nodes.text: Similar to other respiratory viruses, people of extreme ages (the very young and elderly), those with multiple medical & immunocompromised conditions may be at higher risk of severe disease and hospitalisation but in isolation mortality is thought to be relatively uncommon. 3/5

nodes.author: GSRajahram
nodes.text: In temperate climates, particularly during winter, numerous respiratory viruses are usually in co-circulation, resulting in illness and potentially causing co-infections and may result in poorer outcomes (e.g with influenza)

nodes.author: GSRajahram
nodes.text: We have better diagnostic tests to detect this virus & improved surveillance, resulting in better reporting. At the moment, treatment for hMPV is mainly supportive. Lead a healthy lifestyle with optimism, measured precautions, and appropriate protection of the vulnerable. 5/5
